collapses_to.tool: a single idempotency-keyed ingest that takes an attestation — the reviewed input's digest, the outcome, the exceptions, and an owner with a validity period — and creates the evidence record with its expiry already set, instead of a create followed by an update that has to be threaded with the new record's id

idempotency.verified_at: The createEvidence tool description published by https://api.noru.tech/v1/mcp documents creating text/note/link evidence with optional control mappings and states that file uploads are not supported over MCP; it documents no idempotency key, and its published input fields do not include an expiry. The "Idempotency/Upsert Behavior" section of https://api.noru.tech/llms.txt covers assets and security findings only.
idempotency.gap: No idempotency key is documented for evidence, so this piece does not rely on one: it embeds a marker built from the review key and a digest of the rendered attestation in the evidence description, and probes getOrganizationEvidence before creating. A documented key would let the probe go away; a documented expiry field on create would remove the second operation entirely.

idempotency.verified_at: The updateEvidence tool description published by https://api.noru.tech/v1/mcp documents updating an existing evidence record's fields, including its expiry; https://api.noru.tech/llms.txt documents the equivalent REST operation as PATCH /v1/evidence/{id}, "Updates evidence fields". Setting the same field to the same value twice is not documented as having any further effect, but nothing published says so either, so the piece checks first.
idempotency.gap: The record is addressed by an id the piece only learns from the create in the same plan, and no key is documented that would let a later run recognise the record without first probing getOrganizationEvidence for the marker it wrote itself. Until an expiry can be set at creation time, or a documented key exists, this stays a probe plus a dependent call.

source.note: The organization's controls and their status. Ids come from Noru; this plugin ships none.

The full context for one control: what the framework expects, what is already linked, coverage, and the procedure an auditor follows. The difference between expected and linked is the first half of the queue.

Every evidence record linked to a control with its owner, status, type and expiry. The expired and nearly-expired ones are the second half of the queue: a review that went stale is due again, and only Noru knows when.
The catalogue of framework-level evidence-item templates, used to resolve titles and types for items the control context returns by id.

exit_codes.1: drift, validation failure, an expired sign-off under --as-of, missing prerequisite input, or a stale plan
exit_codes.2: usage error, including a push without --confirm
